ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Sujay sees a shooting star go across the night sky, and took a picture of it. The shooting star consists of a star body, which is bounded by four quarter-circle arcs, and a triangular tail. Suppose $AB = 2$, $AC = 4$. Let the area of the shooting star be $X$. If $6X = a-b\pi$ for positive integers $a, b$, find $a + b$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a right-side triangular tail, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, AB is a vertical side, AC is a horizontal side extending rightward from A, and BC is the slanted side. The star body part is attached near AB, and is enclosed by four quarter-circle arcs; the left solid arc is outside triangle ABC, and the right dashed arc is inside the triangular tail. Reasoning: From the problem statement AB=2, AC=4, so the area of the triangular tail ABC is (1/2)·AB·AC=(1/2)·2·4=4. Because AB=2, the radii of the four quarter-circle arcs of the star body are all 1. The right dashed part is inside the triangular tail and does not additionally increase the union area, so it is only necessary to add the area of the left half of the star body outside the triangle to the triangle area. The left half can be decomposed into two 1×1 squares minus two quarter-circles of radius 1, with area 2-2·(π/4)=2-π/2. Therefore X=4+(2-π/2)=6-π/2. Thus 6X=36-3π, so a=36, b=3, a+b=39.

method.method_draft: First describe the full four-arc star body suggested by the diagram: its top and bottom vertices are A and B, and it is symmetric about AB, with two dotted arcs on the right and two solid arcs on the left. Because AB=2, the body fits in a 2-by-2 square made from four unit squares, and the four boundary arcs are quarter-circles of radius 1. Compute the entire four-arc body area as the 2-by-2 square area minus four quarter-circles: 4-π. By symmetry, exactly half of this body lies to the left of AB and half to the right. The right half is drawn inside triangle ABC, so the shooting-star union area equals triangle ABC plus only half of the body: X=1/2·2·4+(4-π)/2=4+2-π/2=6-π/2. Hence 6X=36-3π and a+b=39.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有一个由星体和三角形尾部组成的“流星”图形。左侧星体以竖直线段 AB 为中轴，A 在上、B 在下，星体边界由四段四分之一圆弧组成；左边两段为实线弧，右边两段为虚线弧。右侧是三角形 ABC，AC 从 A 水平向右到 C，BC 从 B 斜向右上到 C，虚线的右半星体位于三角形 ABC 内部。已知 AB=2，AC=4。

推理：因为 AB=2，按图中四段四分之一圆弧的结构，完整星体可放入一个 2×2 的正方形中，该正方形由四个 1×1 小正方形组成，每段边界弧都是半径为 1 的四分之一圆。完整四弧星体面积等于 2×2 正方形面积减去四个半径为 1 的四分之一圆面积，即 4-π。由关于 AB 的对称性，星体左右各占一半面积，所以左半星体面积为 (4-π)/2。三角形 ABC 的面积为 1/2·AB·AC=1/2·2·4=4。由于右半星体在三角形 ABC 内，流星总面积 X 等于三角形 ABC 面积加上左半星体面积：X=4+(4-π)/2=6-π/2。因此 6X=36-3π，所以 a=36，b=3，a+b=39。
